notes: §1985:VI.5.9.5 GR4: 'The ',' (comma), 'B' (space), '0' (zero), and '/' (slant) are used as the insertion characters. The insertion characters are counted in the size of the item and represent the position in the item into which the character will be inserted', and when the comma is the last symbol 'the PICTURE clause must be the last clause of the data description entry and must be immediately followed by the separator period'. CobolEdit.TrySimpleInsertion (set B 0 / and the grouping separator, IsSimpleInsertionSymbol) writes the character at the symbol's own position in Render's first pass, a space for B, and CharacterPositions counts each in the size; under DECIMAL-POINT IS COMMA Format exchanges the two separators, so the period is the simple insertion character. The lexer rule PIC_STRING keeps a final comma only when the separator period follows it and gives a comma followed by a space back as a separator; PictureSeparatorPeriodRule.Violations, run from Frontend.LexAndParseOnce at every edition, refuses a character-string that ends in a comma or period not followed at once by the separator period (COBOL2419). The one 2023 addition, an EDITING character-1, is refused at 85 (COBOL0900). Probed at --std 85: PIC 9B,0/9 edits 12 to '1 ,0/2'; PIC 9,9,9,. edits 123 to '1,2,3,'; PIC 999,, USAGE DISPLAY. and PIC 999,; VALUE ZERO. get COBOL2419; PIC 999, USAGE DISPLAY. is the picture 999; under DECIMAL-POINT IS COMMA, PIC 999.. edits 123 to '123.'. The witness runs B, /, 0, an embedded comma and PIC 999,. as the last clause.
